input:
Earlier scenes:
在古代，很多医生不知道怎么用药。所以他们找到了很多植物对药。神农先看到很多病人，他们吃很多植物对药。但是我觉得他们的吃的植物，让他们病人。神农觉得这个植物可能特别是毒。所以他想找一个植物对药，他们可以吃对药。正好，他找到了一把花，他想把花放在茶里，对药。他不知道如果这把花对你的身体好，这就要看如果这把花毒不毒了。神农想找别的植物，但是这很麻烦。正好，他找到了别的花。他一吃花，很快就生病了。他的肚子疼死了。神农不知道他吃不吃灵芝或者夹竹桃。

This scene:
别的人给了神农一个灵芝。这个植物可以让神农更好。比方说，他会觉得更健康。吃灵芝以后，他可以再走。现在他觉得更好。最后，神农找到了很多植物，他可以用对药。这些植物让神农很高兴。神农想跟很多人分享他的新药。

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 别的人给了神农一个灵芝：另外一个人，“别的” is for “a different type”, and “all else except the spoken one”, whereas “另外“ is for “addition in quantity”, and “another, the other”
- 这个植物可以让神农更好：身体更好
- 比方说，他会觉得更健康：比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it
- 吃灵芝以后，他可以再走：吃了，了completed; 又可以走了

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 别的人：别人，Use “别人” for other people in general when no specific group is being contrasted; “别的人” normally contrasts with an already mentioned group of people. [teacher rule: bieren]
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 一个灵芝：一株灵芝，“株” is the suitable measure word for a whole medicinal fungus or plant; “个” is too general here. [rule: none]
3. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 很多植物，他可以用对药：很多可以用来做药的植物，“用对药” means using medicine correctly and cannot describe plants that can serve as medicine; “用来做药” states the plants’ purpose. [rule: none]
4. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 这个植物可以让神农更好：它可以让神农更好，Use a pronoun for an object mentioned in the immediately preceding sentence when no other possible referent competes with it. [rule: redundancy_delete]
5. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 最后，神农找到了很多植物：最后，他找到了很多植物，Use a pronoun when the same character has just been mentioned and no other character has intervened. [rule: redundancy_delete]
6. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 吃灵芝以后：吃了灵芝以后，The eating is a completed action before the later ability to continue walking, so it needs completed-action “了.” [rule: aspect_le_completed]

items.reason: “别的人” is wrong for one additional person here, but “别人” means other people generally rather than “另外一个人.”
“一个灵芝” is an acceptable measure-word phrase, although “一株灵芝” is also correct.
Plants cannot be described as “用对药”; “可以用来做药的植物” correctly expresses plants usable for making medicine.
The recently introduced lingzhi should be referred to as “它,” but the corrected sentence still needs “身体更好” rather than “神农更好.”
Shennong has just been referred to, so the close repeated reference should be “他” rather than his name.
The eating is completed before the later action, so “吃了灵芝以后” is correct.
